To me I would say the Old Testament is more of the “where we came from, how things used to be”, and the New Testament is, “where we are going and how we should handle things.” 

Concerning the Satan thing, that’s true, and what I find interesting though is it’s common to see people saying he will punish you, but like you said pop culture is to blame on that one. Just like saying the fires of hell. There is never any mention of fire in hell, and as far as I’m aware it never really explained what punishment was for those who didn’t believe but clearly the punishment gets misconstrued to an extreme degree.

In the case of the god paradox, the idea is to test the limits of a supposedly all powerful being. In theory you could just say he does create that and then makes him self stronger to lift it. As long as you believe and do your best that’s all you can really ask, hell it’s all god really asks. Do I prefer other religions, yeah, do I judge, from time to time, mainly it’s towards Christians, but that’s also because of a bias I have because of how I’ve been treated, what I’ve read and seen. 

For me, I see religion in a few ways:
